cards.front: What happens in the eye during accommodation for near vision?
cards.back: **Parasympathetic** fibers (CN III, via the ciliary ganglion) contract the **ciliary muscle**. This **relaxes the zonules**, so the lens becomes **rounder** and bends light more. The near response also includes **convergence** and **miosis**.
cards.back_pt: Fibras **parassimpáticas** (NC III, via gânglio ciliar) contraem o **músculo ciliar**. Isso **relaxa as fibras zonulares**, e o cristalino fica **mais arredondado** e refrata mais a luz. A resposta para perto inclui também **convergência** e **miose**.

cards.front: How does light change the membrane potential of a rod?
cards.back: Light converts **11-cis-retinal** to all-trans-retinal in rhodopsin. Transducin activates **phosphodiesterase**, **cGMP falls**, cGMP-gated Na channels close, and the rod **hyperpolarizes**. It then releases **less glutamate**. Retinal comes from **vitamin A**.
cards.back_pt: A luz converte o **11-cis-retinal** em all-trans-retinal na rodopsina. A transducina ativa a **fosfodiesterase**, o **GMPc cai**, os canais de Na dependentes de GMPc se fecham e o bastonete **hiperpolariza**. Ele então libera **menos glutamato**. O retinal vem da **vitamina A**.

cards.front: Where is the lesion in an upper vs a lower homonymous quadrantanopia?
cards.back: **Upper** (*pie in the sky*): **temporal lobe**, the inferior optic radiation fibers (**Meyer loop**). **Lower** (*pie on the floor*): **parietal lobe**, the superior optic radiation fibers. Both lesions are **contralateral** to the field defect.
cards.back_pt: **Superior** (*pie in the sky*): **lobo temporal**, fibras inferiores da radiação óptica (**alça de Meyer**). **Inferior** (*pie on the floor*): **lobo parietal**, fibras superiores da radiação óptica. As duas lesões são **contralaterais** ao defeito de campo.

cards.front: What does the swinging flashlight test show with a left optic nerve lesion?
cards.back: Light in the right eye constricts **both** pupils. When the light swings to the left eye, both pupils **dilate**, because less signal reaches the midbrain. This is a **relative afferent pupillary defect** (Marcus Gunn pupil); the CN III efferent pathway is intact.
cards.back_pt: A luz no olho direito contrai **as duas** pupilas. Quando a luz passa para o olho esquerdo, as duas pupilas **dilatam**, porque chega menos sinal ao mesencéfalo. É um **defeito pupilar aferente relativo** (pupila de Marcus Gunn); a via eferente do NC III está íntegra.

cards.front: Why does a compressive CN III palsy affect the pupil, while a diabetic CN III palsy often spares it?
cards.back: Pupil fibers run on the **outside** of CN III. **Compression** (e.g., posterior communicating artery **aneurysm**) hits them early: **dilated pupil**. **Diabetic ischemia** damages the center of the nerve: eye **down and out**, ptosis, pupil **spared**.
cards.back_pt: As fibras pupilares ficam na **periferia** do NC III. A **compressão** (ex.: **aneurisma** da artéria comunicante posterior) as atinge cedo: **pupila dilatada**. A **isquemia diabética** lesa o centro do nervo: olho **para baixo e para fora**, ptose, pupila **poupada**.

cards.front: How does primary open-angle glaucoma present?
cards.back: It is **painless** and slow, usually in both eyes. Optic nerve damage causes **peripheral** (arcuate) field loss first, often unnoticed. The fundus shows **optic disc cupping** (a larger cup-to-disc ratio). Intraocular pressure is **often** high but can be normal.
cards.back_pt: É **indolor** e lento, geralmente bilateral. A lesão do nervo óptico causa primeiro perda de campo **periférico** (arqueada), muitas vezes despercebida. O fundo de olho mostra **escavação do disco óptico** (relação escavação/disco maior). A pressão intraocular **costuma** estar alta, mas pode ser normal.

cards.front: How do central retinal artery occlusion and central retinal vein occlusion look on fundoscopy?
cards.back: **Artery** occlusion: a pale, swollen retina with a **cherry-red spot** at the fovea (the choroid shows through). **Vein** occlusion: diffuse **hemorrhages**, dilated tortuous veins and disc swelling (*blood and thunder*). Both cause sudden painless monocular loss.
cards.back_pt: Oclusão da **artéria**: retina pálida e edemaciada com **mancha vermelho-cereja** na fóvea (a coroide aparece por transparência). Oclusão da **veia**: **hemorragias** difusas, veias dilatadas e tortuosas e edema do disco (*blood and thunder*). Ambas causam perda visual monocular súbita e indolor.

cards.front: How do BPPV, vestibular neuritis and Ménière disease differ in timing?
cards.back: **BPPV**: seconds, triggered by head position (loose otoconia in a semicircular canal). **Vestibular neuritis**: constant vertigo for **days**, hearing normal. **Ménière**: attacks lasting **hours**, with tinnitus, ear fullness and fluctuating hearing loss (**endolymphatic hydrops**).
cards.back_pt: **VPPB**: segundos, desencadeada pela posição da cabeça (otocônias soltas em um canal semicircular). **Neurite vestibular**: vertigem contínua por **dias**, audição normal. **Ménière**: crises que duram **horas**, com zumbido, plenitude auricular e perda auditiva flutuante (**hidropisia endolinfática**).

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man has had headaches for 2 months. His wife says he sometimes has trouble finding words. On confrontation testing, he cannot see objects in the upper right quadrant of the visual field of either eye. The lower fields are normal. Visual acuity and pupillary light reflexes are normal. MRI shows a mass. Where is the lesion most likely located?
choices: Left optic nerve
Optic chiasm
Left optic tract
Left temporal lobe
Left parietal lobe
questions.explanation: A right **upper homonymous quadrantanopia** (*pie in the sky*) points to the left **temporal lobe**. There, the inferior optic radiation fibers (**Meyer loop**) carry the upper half of the contralateral field. A left parietal lesion damages the superior radiation fibers and causes a **lower** quadrantanopia instead. An optic tract lesion causes a complete homonymous hemianopia.
questions.explanation_pt: Uma **quadrantanopsia homônima superior** direita (*pie in the sky*) indica lesão no **lobo temporal** esquerdo. Ali, as fibras inferiores da radiação óptica (**alça de Meyer**) levam a metade superior do campo contralateral. Uma lesão parietal esquerda atinge as fibras superiores da radiação e causa quadrantanopsia **inferior**. Uma lesão do trato óptico causa hemianopsia homônima completa.

questions.stem: A 32-year-old woman has had slowly worsening hearing loss in her left ear for 2 years. It became worse during a recent pregnancy. Her mother needed hearing aids from age 40. The ear canals and tympanic membranes look normal. There is no ear discharge or history of ear infections. When a vibrating tuning fork is placed on the middle of her forehead, she hears it louder in the left ear. On the left, she hears the fork better on the mastoid bone than next to the ear canal. On the right, air conduction is better than bone conduction. What is the most likely cause of her hearing loss?
choices: Vestibular schwannoma at the left cerebellopontine angle
Fixation of the left stapes footplate by abnormal bone
Endolymphatic hydrops of the left inner ear
Loss of hair cells at the base of the left cochlea
Cholesteatoma of the left middle ear
questions.explanation: Weber louder in the left ear plus bone better than air on the left means **left conductive hearing loss**. A young woman with a family history, worsening in pregnancy and a normal tympanic membrane fits **otosclerosis**: new bone fixes the **stapes** to the oval window. A **vestibular schwannoma** is the tempting unilateral cause, but it causes **sensorineural** loss, so Weber would go to the right ear and Rinne would stay air > bone. Cholesteatoma is also conductive, but it usually shows an abnormal tympanic membrane and ear discharge.
questions.explanation_pt: Weber mais alto à esquerda e condução óssea melhor que a aérea à esquerda indicam **perda auditiva condutiva esquerda**. O quadro (mulher jovem, história familiar, piora na gestação e membrana timpânica normal) sugere **otosclerose**: osso novo fixa o **estribo** à janela oval. O **schwannoma vestibular** é a causa unilateral tentadora, mas causa perda **neurossensorial**: o Weber lateralizaria para a direita e o Rinne continuaria com via aérea > óssea. O colesteatoma também é condutivo, mas costuma mostrar membrana timpânica alterada e otorreia.

questions.stem: A 67-year-old woman comes to the emergency department with severe pain in her right eye, headache, nausea and vomiting. The pain began this evening in a dark movie theater. Two days ago she started oxybutynin for urge incontinence. She sees colored halos around lights. The right eye is red, the cornea is cloudy, and the pupil is mid-dilated and does not react to light. The eye feels very hard on palpation. Which mechanism best explains her condition?
choices: Gradual increase in resistance to aqueous outflow through an open trabecular meshwork
Inflammation of the iris and ciliary body
Embolic occlusion of the central retinal artery
Separation of the neurosensory retina from the pigment epithelium
Forward bowing of the peripheral iris that blocks aqueous outflow at the trabecular meshwork
questions.explanation: In **acute angle-closure glaucoma**, a mid-dilated pupil (darkness and an **anticholinergic** drug) increases iris-lens contact, so aqueous builds up behind the iris and pushes the peripheral iris against the trabecular meshwork. Aqueous cannot drain, intraocular pressure rises fast, and corneal edema causes **halos**. **Open-angle glaucoma** often involves high pressure, but it is painless and slow. Anterior uveitis causes a red, painful eye, but with a **small** pupil.
questions.explanation_pt: No **glaucoma agudo de ângulo fechado**, a pupila em médio-midríase (escuro e um fármaco **anticolinérgico**) aumenta o contato entre a íris e o cristalino; o humor aquoso se acumula atrás da íris e empurra a íris periférica contra a malha trabecular. O aquoso não drena, a pressão intraocular sobe rapidamente e o edema de córnea causa **halos**. O **glaucoma de ângulo aberto** costuma ter pressão alta, mas é indolor e lento. A uveíte anterior causa olho vermelho e doloroso, porém com pupila **pequena**.

questions.stem: A 4-month-old boy is brought for a well-child visit. He feeds well on breast milk and is growing normally. He has no jaundice and no hepatomegaly. Examination shows bilateral lens opacities, and the red reflex is reduced in both eyes. His urine is positive for a reducing sugar that is not glucose. Blood galactose is high. Which substance most likely builds up in his lenses and causes the cataracts?
choices: Sorbitol
Galactose-1-phosphate
Galactitol
Fructose-1-phosphate
Glucocerebroside
questions.explanation: This is **galactokinase deficiency**: galactose cannot be phosphorylated, so **aldose reductase** turns it into **galactitol**. Galactitol is osmotically active, pulls water into the lens and causes **cataracts**. **Galactose-1-phosphate** is the tempting choice, but it builds up only in classic galactosemia (GALT deficiency), where it damages the liver, kidney and brain; even there, the cataracts come from galactitol. Sorbitol is the same pathway acting on glucose in diabetes.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se de **deficiência de galactoquinase**: a galactose não pode ser fosforilada, então a **aldose redutase** a converte em **galactitol**. O galactitol é osmoticamente ativo, atrai água para o cristalino e causa **catarata**. A **galactose-1-fosfato** é a alternativa tentadora, mas só se acumula na galactosemia clássica (deficiência de GALT), onde lesa fígado, rim e cérebro; mesmo ali, a catarata vem do galactitol. O sorbitol é a mesma via agindo sobre a glicose no diabetes.

notes.title: Special senses: eye and ear
notes.body_md:
## Optics and retina

- Near vision: **parasympathetic** input (CN III) contracts the **ciliary muscle**, the **zonules relax** and the lens rounds up.
- Light lowers **cGMP** in rods and cones, and the cell **hyperpolarizes**. Rods: dim light, no color. Cones: color, fovea.
- **Vitamin A** deficiency: **night blindness**.

## Visual field lesions

- Optic nerve: **monocular** loss. Chiasm: **bitemporal hemianopia** (pituitary mass).
- Optic tract: contralateral **homonymous hemianopia**.
- **Meyer loop** (temporal lobe): contralateral **upper** quadrantanopia. Parietal radiation: **lower** quadrantanopia.
- **PCA** stroke: homonymous hemianopia with **macular sparing**.

## Pupils and eye movements

- Light reflex: CN II → pretectum → both **Edinger-Westphal** nuclei → CN III. Optic nerve disease gives a **relative afferent pupillary defect**.
- **Argyll Robertson** pupil (neurosyphilis): reacts to near targets, not to light.
- **Horner syndrome**: ptosis, miosis, anhidrosis; causes include a **Pancoast tumor** and carotid dissection.
- **CN IV** palsy: vertical diplopia. **CN VI** palsy: the eye cannot abduct.
- **INO** (MLF lesion, often MS): the eye on the lesion side cannot adduct; the other eye has nystagmus on abduction.

## Eye disease

- **Open-angle glaucoma**: painless, slow, **cupped disc**. **Angle-closure**: painful red eye, halos, fixed mid-dilated pupil; an emergency.
- **Cataract**: age, diabetes (**sorbitol**), galactosemia (**galactitol**), corticosteroids.
- **AMD**: dry (drusen, slow) vs wet (new choroidal vessels, fast).
- **Retinal detachment**: flashes, floaters, a curtain over vision.
- **CRAO**: **cherry-red spot** (also seen in Tay-Sachs). **CRVO**: widespread hemorrhages.
- **Papilledema**: both discs, high intracranial pressure. **Optic neuritis**: one eye, pain on eye movement, MS.
- **Retinoblastoma** (*RB1*): **leukocoria** in a child. **Anterior uveitis**: **HLA-B27**.

## Ear and balance

- **Conductive** loss: Weber goes to the affected ear; Rinne bone > air in the affected ear. **Sensorineural**: Weber goes to the normal ear; Rinne air > bone.
- Conductive causes: **otosclerosis**, **cholesteatoma**, otitis media (*S. pneumoniae*, nontypeable *H. influenzae*, *M. catarrhalis*).
- Sensorineural causes: **presbycusis** and **noise** (both damage hair cells at the cochlear **base**: high tones lost first), **vestibular schwannoma**.
- **Central** vertigo: vertical or direction-changing nystagmus and other brainstem signs.
notes.body_pt_md:
## Óptica e retina

- Visão de perto: o estímulo **parassimpático** (NC III) contrai o **músculo ciliar**, as **fibras zonulares relaxam** e o cristalino se arredonda.
- A luz reduz o **GMPc** em bastonetes e cones, e a célula **hiperpolariza**. Bastonetes: pouca luz, sem cor. Cones: cor, fóvea.
- Deficiência de **vitamina A**: **cegueira noturna**.

## Lesões do campo visual

- Nervo óptico: perda **monocular**. Quiasma: **hemianopsia bitemporal** (massa hipofisária).
- Trato óptico: **hemianopsia homônima** contralateral.
- **Alça de Meyer** (lobo temporal): quadrantanopsia **superior** contralateral. Radiação parietal: quadrantanopsia **inferior**.
- AVC da **ACP**: hemianopsia homônima com **preservação macular**.

## Pupilas e movimentos oculares

- Reflexo fotomotor: NC II → área pré-tectal → ambos os núcleos de **Edinger-Westphal** → NC III. Doença do nervo óptico causa **defeito pupilar aferente relativo**.
- Pupila de **Argyll Robertson** (neurossífilis): reage à acomodação, não à luz.
- **Síndrome de Horner**: ptose, miose, anidrose; causas incluem **tumor de Pancoast** e dissecção carotídea.
- Paralisia do **NC IV**: diplopia vertical. Paralisia do **NC VI**: o olho não abduz.
- **OIN** (lesão do FLM, frequentemente EM): o olho do lado da lesão não aduz; o outro olho tem nistagmo na abdução.

## Doenças oculares

- **Glaucoma de ângulo aberto**: indolor, lento, **escavação do disco**. **Ângulo fechado**: olho vermelho e doloroso, halos, pupila fixa em médio-midríase; uma emergência.
- **Catarata**: idade, diabetes (**sorbitol**), galactosemia (**galactitol**), corticoides.
- **DMRI**: seca (drusas, lenta) vs úmida (neovasos de coroide, rápida).
- **Descolamento de retina**: fotopsias, moscas volantes, uma cortina sobre a visão.
- **OACR**: **mancha vermelho-cereja** (também vista na doença de Tay-Sachs). **OVCR**: hemorragias difusas.
- **Papiledema**: ambos os discos, hipertensão intracraniana. **Neurite óptica**: um olho, dor à movimentação ocular, EM.
- **Retinoblastoma** (*RB1*): **leucocoria** em criança. **Uveíte anterior**: **HLA-B27**.

## Ouvido e equilíbrio

- Perda **condutiva**: Weber lateraliza para o ouvido afetado; Rinne óssea > aérea no ouvido afetado. **Neurossensorial**: Weber lateraliza para o ouvido normal; Rinne aérea > óssea.
- Causas condutivas: **otosclerose**, **colesteatoma**, otite média (*S. pneumoniae*, *H. influenzae* não tipável, *M. catarrhalis*).
- Causas neurossensoriais: **presbiacusia** e **ruído** (ambos lesam células ciliadas na **base** da cóclea: perda primeiro dos sons agudos), **schwannoma vestibular**.
- Vertigem **central**: nistagmo vertical ou que muda de direção e outros sinais de tronco encefálico.
